mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day returns in low FEDFUNDS periods (FEDFUNDS < 4.0%) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals an economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day returns in high UNRATE periods (UNRATE > 5.0%) are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicate a tightening monetary policy cycle, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day returns in periods of simultaneous FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rising are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A late-cycle expansion regime defined by GDP growth above 11200 billion dollars (GDPC1) and unemployment below 4.5% (UNRATE) indicates an overheating economy, leading to market overvaluation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day returns in late-cycle expansion periods (GDPC1>11200 and UNRATE<4.5%) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity and corporate profitability, supporting positive equity valuations and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day returns in high INDPRO periods (INDPRO > 110.0) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate below 2200.0 thousand units (HOUST) signals weak consumer demand and economic contraction, reducing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day returns in low HOUST periods (HOUST < 2200.0) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) combined with falling housing starts (HOUST) indicates a dual stress of inflation and weak housing demand, signaling an economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day returns in periods of CPIAUCSL rising and HOUST falling are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle defined by federal funds rate above 4.5% (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index above 2.0% annualized (CPIAUCSL) increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day returns in monetary tightening periods (FEDFUNDS>4.5% and CPIAUCSL>2.0%) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
